audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Gwen Levels 2-3 and 2+ items, while the prose says levels 1-3 are 'genuinely even', 4-5 is 'my worst window' and 'This is where the EVEN lane tilts back to him'.
The full layer's phase rows were template text and named no Yasuo ability except Last Breath.
audit.why: Packet flags 'never names any of Yasuo's abilities'. His real gates are Wind Wall at 17-25s and the two-stack Steel Tempest; Gwen's are Level 6 and Riftmaker before Infinity Edge.
audit.corrected: Way of the Wanderer, Steel Tempest, Wind Wall, Sweeping Blade and Last Breath now named with cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer says Wind Wall eats 'any Q snip you cast through it' in three places, and the full layer never mentions Wind Wall at all despite it being the defining interaction.
audit.why: Riot on Wind Wall: 'Creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds.' Gwen's Needlework is flagged as a projectile in her kit file ('can be blocked by Wind Wall-class effects'), so the wall eats her ultimate. Snip Snip! carries no projectile flag — Riot describes it as a cone of up to six snips — so it is not blocked, and telling the player otherwise removes her main damage tool for no reason. Riot on Last Breath: it 'Blinks to an Airborne enemy champion', so refusing the two-stack Steel Tempest knockup denies his ultimate entirely. Riot on Sweeping Blade: 'Cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds', which is why denying him minions breaks the dash chain.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall blocks Needlework but not the cone; the Airborne requirement on Last Breath and the Sweeping Blade re-cast rule written into both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Last Breath was the only tracked cooldown.
audit.why: Wind Wall 25/23/21/19/17s is the punishable one; Steel Tempest is a flat 4s and Sweeping Blade 0.5 down to 0.1s.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall is now the tracked cooldown, with its 4-second duration.

edits.before: Level 1-3 is genuinely even and it's all about respecting Windwall. Never throw an R volley or cast a Snip Snip at range into the wall, because it eats both, and Yasuo can predrop it the moment you wind up. I trade by walking up and dropping the Q cone right on top of him at melee, where he can't wall six snips in time, and I lean on the true-damage center snip to chunk him. I have no mist and no E reset value yet, so I just contest CS and avoid eating a full E-dash into Q3 knockup while his flow shield is up.
edits.after: Level 1-3 is genuinely even and it's all about respecting Wind Wall. Never throw an R volley into it — the wall blocks projectiles for four seconds and eats every needle — but Snip Snip! is a cone, not a projectile, so it cuts through. I trade by walking up and dropping the Q cone right on top of him at melee, and I lean on the true-damage center snip to chunk him. I have no mist and no E reset value yet, so I just contest CS and avoid eating a full E-dash into a two-stack Steel Tempest knockup while his flow shield is up.

notes: Wind Wall was never mentioned in the full layer at all — the same class of gap as the Azir/Yasuo calibration example. Worse, the content layer told the player Wind Wall also blocks Snip Snip!; Gwen's kit flags the projectile on Needlework only, and Riot describes Snip Snip! as a cone, so the wall does not stop her main damage. Last Breath requiring an Airborne target (refuse the two-stack Steel Tempest and the ultimate is dead) was also absent.
